title: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of collapse models in the strongly non-Gaussian regime
summary: Standard objective collapse models offer a unified approach to the quantum measurement problem but predict an unphysical, indefinite increase in the energy of the system. The dissipative Diósi-Penrose (dDP) model resolves this heating issue by introducing a linear friction mechanism. However, this modification induces complex, non-Gaussian phase-space dynamics. We rigorously establish the thermodynamic consistency of this friction mechanism -- extended to the CSL model -- across both weakly and strongly non-Gaussian regimes.
